contract: Capacity is three units. A queued request may reserve units before its delivery callback runs. Cancellation before delivery must return all reserved units; a later delivery callback must not transfer a cancelled reservation. Live delivered owners release their own units once.

evidenceRequirements.description: Establish any valid causal witness from the supplied code and context; exact driver numbers/order are not required. One evaluator-only witness: A three-unit holder blocks a two-unit request. Releasing the holder reserves two units and posts delivery. Cancellation in that handoff window removes the waiter but fails to roll back its reservation; delivery then skips it. A new two-unit request cannot be admitted despite no live owner. Returning reserved units on cancellation restores progress.

Explain at least one relevant boundary or benign path inferable from the supplied code/context; the following evaluator examples are alternatives, not a mandatory unseen checklist: Cancellation while still queued reserves nothing; delivered releases work; repeated cancel/release cannot over-credit; normal handoff admits the waiter; outer cleanup is an explicit alternative owner, not an assumed automatic fix.
The pre-delivery reservation owner: does cancel terminate and release the reservation, or does an outer scope retain responsibility until its explicit cleanup call?
